description: We are trying to find an innovative solution for our Earth.
summary:
FieldPulse is a data-driven agricultural decision-support platform designed to help farmers and agronomists adapt to changing climate conditions. By selecting a specific field location and current crop, users access localized historical climate data including temperature, rainfall, and soil moisture compared against a multi-year baseline to identify clear environmental shifts.

To address the challenge of unpredictable yields and guesswork in farming, FieldPulse combines climate trend analysis with an evidence-based soil health diagnosis and risk-zone mapping. Crucially, the platform tailors its actionable recommendations along with clear reasoning to the user’s specific priority, whether that is conserving water, restoring soil health, or maximizing income.

FieldPulse is vital because it bridges the gap between complex meteorological numbers and practical field decisions, empowering growers to take targeted action on irrigation, soil testing, and crop diversification before yields suffer.
details:
What It Does & How It Works FieldPulse

is a climate-smart agricultural decision-support web platform that transforms satellite Earth observations into practical farming strategies. Users start by selecting their exact field coordinates on an interactive map and specifying their current crop (e.g., wheat). The platform then builds a 10-year "Field Fingerprint" by comparing recent environmental trends such as surface soil wetness, annual rainfall, growing-season temperature, and vegetation vitality (NDVI) against a historical multi-year baseline (2016–2020) to calculate an overall agricultural stress score. Next, it runs an automated Soil Health Diagnosis to flag potential risks and suggest evidence-based treatments. Finally, an interactive 5-year Decision Simulator allows users to adjust their personal priorities Water Conservation, Soil Health, and Income/Forage to compare tailored crop rotation strategies (such as adding cover crops or rotating with faba beans or sorghum) alongside clear NASA evidence, risk warnings, and confidence levels.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Rather than overwhelming growers with raw meteorological numbers, FieldPulse translates complex data into clear discussion signals that replace guesswork with proactive planning. Its primary benefit is enabling customized, resilient crop rotations before climate stress severely degrades yields. In the long term, the project aims to help smallholder farmers and agronomists optimize scarce water resources, prevent soil degradation, and sustain farm profitability under escalating climate pressure.

Tools, Data & Technologies Used

  • Earth Observation Data: Powered by NASA Earth observations, including NASA POWER live meteorological APIs (surface soil wetness GWETTOP, air temperature T2M, and precipitation PRECTOTCORR) and NASA GIBS / MODIS Terra NDVI satellite imagery layers.
  • Mapping & Frontend: Built as a responsive web application using modern frontend web technologies (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript) integrated with Leaflet.js and OpenStreetMap for interactive geolocation and geospatial visualization.

Creativity & Innovation

Most agricultural tools either display raw satellite charts that require technical expertise to interpret or act as rigid black-box predictors. FieldPulse is uniquely creative because it combines explainable multi-year resilience scoring with user-weighted priority sliders dynamically re-ranking crop rotation pathways based on what matters most to the farmer while transparently showing the exact satellite evidence and local risks behind every recommendation.

Key Factors Considered by Our Team

  • Transparency & Trust: Clearly communicating data limitations, confidence levels, and local validation needs (e.g., reminding users that satellite estimates complement rather than replace physical soil tests and local agronomic expertise).
  • Usability & Accessibility: Designing a clean, jargon-free interface with built-in metric explainers ("How to read this") so non-technical users can interpret indicators effortlessly.
  • Real-World Trade-offs: Balancing ecological sustainability (water and soil health) with economic viability (income and equipment continuity) so recommendations remain practical for real farms.
